question.problem: A writer is editing the first draft of a book. On average, there have been $4$ typos per page. What is the probability of finding $2$ typos on the next page? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that typos occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of typos on a page of the book. Since the average rate is $4$ typos per page, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of typos can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =4,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(4).$

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{4}^{x}{e}^{-4}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability of finding $2$ typos on the next page is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=2) & =f(2) \\  & =\frac{{4}^{2}{e}^{-4}}{2!} \\  & ≈0.147\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
